subject.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full

question: Should `security=full` bypass the ambiguous-interpreter fail-closed heuristic for approval-gated ask modes, or should that bypass remain limited to ask-off YOLO?
rationale: The code change is mechanically small, but it changes the exec trust boundary beyond the current shipped docs and the linked issue already carries security and product-decision labels.

options.title: Gate on security-policy signoff
options.body: Require an owner decision, then rebase and align both exec docs to the accepted policy before merge.

options.title: Keep YOLO-only
options.body: Preserve the current ask-off-only bypass and close or revise this PR if approval-gated sessions should retain fail-closed interpreter handling.

options.title: Accept broader full-security trust
options.body: Land the broader bypass after maintainers explicitly accept that `security=full` means trust regardless of ask mode.

recommendation.title: Gate on security-policy signoff
recommendation.body: Require an owner decision, then rebase and align both exec docs to the accepted policy before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the host-exec YOLO/default-policy and no-extra-prefilter docs that define the current boundary being expanded.
